spec_features.spec_quote: Turn & wall budgets cap the worst case per episode (`max_turns`, `wall_budget_s`)
spec_features.evidence: tool_loop.py:190 `for turn in range(task.max_turns)` bounds the loop; else clause at line 246-247 sets terminated_reason='turn_budget'. wall: lines 191-193 `if time.time() - start > wall_budget_s: tx.terminated_reason='wall_budget'; break`. Wired from config: run_eval.py:124 `wall_budget = cfg.get('wall_budget_s', 600)` passed at :138 into run_one->run_episode (:81). task.max_turns is a real per-task value (task_specs.py:52,120,...). Both budgets are checked and break/terminate the loop.
spec_features.notes: Both budgets are genuinely enforced end-to-end. wall_budget_s is config-driven; max_turns comes from each TaskSpec.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Enforce a hard turn budget and a wall-clock budget for cost control. (tool_loop.py docstring); config default.yaml: '# Hard budgets (cost control).'

spec_features.spec_quote: when the model emits a give-up phrase with no tool call, stop spending tokens immediately
spec_features.evidence: tool_loop.py:216-220: `if looks_like_give_up(text) and not tool_calls:` appends a record and `tx.terminated_reason='model_gave_up'; break`. looks_like_give_up (line 157) matches GIVE_UP_MARKERS (line 149). The break actually halts the loop, so no further model calls occur.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely enforced: a give-up phrase with no tool call breaks the loop. The mechanism is purely about stopping token spend; it does not soften treatment or debrief the subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Early give-up termination (saves tokens; judge still scores transcript). (tool_loop.py:215); also 'we want the loop to terminate early when the model has clearly quit, to save tokens.' (tool_loop.py:152-154)
